title: API Design for AI Features — Choose Synchronous or Asynchronous Work
key_insight: Synchronous endpoints return the result directly. Asynchronous endpoints create a job ID, then expose status and result retrieval or callbacks.
body:
## Choose Synchronous or Asynchronous Work

A short classification finishes during one request, but a long document job outlives normal network timeouts.

Synchronous endpoints return the result directly. Asynchronous endpoints create a job ID, then expose status and result retrieval or callbacks.

Make status states clear: queued, running, succeeded, failed, and cancelled. Define how long results and logs remain available.
common_mistakes: Clients should parse arbitrary prose as an API contract.
A retry should always create another paid job.
Model changes can never affect API behavior.
mini_exercise: Draw “Choose Synchronous or Asynchronous Work” as three steps and explain each one.
real_world_usage: A stable product API hides model churn and gives clients clear states, errors, and versioned behavior.
explain_back_prompt: Use “Choose Synchronous or Asynchronous Work” to explain API Design for AI Features plainly.
